label: EU(7)-PIM: clonidine, methyldopa, moxonidine and related medicines
title: Clonidine, methyldopa, moxonidine or a related medicine in an older person
statement: Reserpine, methyldopa, clonidine, guanfacine, moxonidine and rilmenidine are named in the EU(7)-PIM list as potentially inappropriate medicines for older people. The reason given for each is a risk of low blood pressure on standing, a slow heart rate, fainting, and effects on the brain such as sedation, depression and poorer thinking. The list advises starting low and changing the dose gradually when starting or stopping reserpine or methyldopa. It gives similar advice for clonidine used for hypertension. Its starting-dose advice for guanfacine concerns the immediate-release form. It gives kidney precautions for reserpine, methyldopa, moxonidine and rilmenidine. As alternatives it suggests other blood pressure medicines, for example ACE inhibitors, or other medicine groups chosen to suit the patient's other conditions. The published entry also gives dose notes, which are not repeated here. This is the entrant's plain-words summary of the list entry, not the published wording.

source.modification_notice: Adapted by the entrant: the statement is a plain-words summary of six rows of the source table (reserpine, methyldopa, clonidine, guanfacine, moxonidine and rilmenidine). The published wording is not reproduced, because the source marks part of it as taken from Micromedex and the right to reuse that part is not settled. The authors have not reviewed this adaptation.

plain_summary: Medicines that lower blood pressure by acting on the brain, such as clonidine, methyldopa and moxonidine, can cause dizziness on standing, a slow pulse, fainting, drowsiness, low mood and confusion in older people.

medicine_groups.name: Centrally acting blood pressure medicines named in the list
medicine_groups.note: Tablets and injections count. Reserpine and rilmenidine are named in the source but are not sold in Australia. Intuniv is guanfacine for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and is rarely used in older people. Apraclonidine (Iopidine) and brimonidine (Alphagan) are eye drops for glaucoma. They are different medicines and do not count. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Normatens is an Australian brand of moxonidine.

rule_for_models: At age 65 or older, one systemic supply of clonidine, methyldopa, moxonidine, guanfacine, reserpine or rilmenidine at any dose is enough for a finding, including a clonidine patch used for systemic treatment. Exclude people known to be under 65, creams, gels or ointments intended only for local use, other local-only preparations, and apraclonidine or brimonidine eye drops. If the supply could otherwise count but age or preparation is unclear, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm what is missing. Count a Normatens tablet as moxonidine even when the record gives only the brand.
cannot_be_seen: Why the medicine was prescribed, for example blood pressure, hot flushes or pain. Also the patient's blood pressure lying and standing, pulse rate and kidney function, whether the patient has had dizziness, fainting, falls, drowsiness, low mood or confusion, and supplies from a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether this medicine is still the best choice at the patient's age, and whether the patient has had dizziness on standing, a slow pulse, fainting, drowsiness, low mood or confusion.
